claude.sample_unit: LLM responses (10 questions x 4 models x 2 prompt types)

links.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and acceptability of LLM answers to TKA patient FAQs against surgeon judgment
links.effect: Only 48.8% (156/320) of ratings deemed acceptable; mean accuracy 3.38 and comprehensiveness 3.48; Gemini and Claude inaccuracies contradicted guidelines.
links.quote: Among all responses assessed by the four reviewers, 48.8% (156/320) were deemed acceptable.

links.outcome: Acceptability of deployed public LLM configurations on intended-use patient education questions
links.effect: Acceptability ranged from 25% (Claude zero-shot) to 77.5% (GPT-4 role-play); many responses judged not safe as sole patient information.
links.quote: While the average accuracy and comprehensiveness ratings were 3.38 and 3.48, respectively, only 48.8% (156/320) of responses were judged acceptable.

links.outcome: Response quality under different prompt framing (zero-shot vs role-play persona) for equivalent questions
links.effect: Role-play significantly improved all metrics for GPT-3.5 (accuracy P=0.020, comprehensiveness P=0.026, acceptability P=0.012) and GPT-4 acceptability (P=0.033); no significant effect for Gemini or Claude.
links.quote: However, no significant improvements were observed for Google Gemini or Claude 3 Opus when using role-playing prompts.

links.outcome: Accuracy, comprehensiveness, acceptability with role-playing prompt template vs zero-shot prompting
links.effect: GPT-3.5 acceptability rose from 45% to 72.5% and GPT-4 from 55% to 77.5% with role-play; GPT-3.5 accuracy 3.33 to 3.70. Effects not significant for Gemini or Claude.
links.quote: Role-playing prompts also significantly enhanced the acceptability rate of ChatGPT-4 ( P = 0.033).

links.outcome: Comparison of four candidate LLMs on the same questions rated by surgeons
links.effect: GPT-4 zero-shot had higher accuracy and comprehensiveness than Gemini (P=0.031, 0.009) and Claude 3 Opus (P=0.019, 0.002), and higher acceptability than Claude (P=0.006).
links.quote: ChatGPT-4 demonstrated significantly higher accuracy and comprehensiveness scores compared to both Google Gemini ( P = 0.031 and P = 0.009, respectively) and Claude 3 Opus ( P = 0.019 and P = 0.002, respectively).

links.outcome: Comprehensibility of LLM answers for patients, per evaluator comments
links.effect: No formal readability analysis; some comments noted Claude zero-shot was hard for patients to understand, while GPT-3.5 role-play was 'very friendly and easy to understand'; comprehension impact of added detail uncertain.
links.quote: This study focused on clinical accuracy and relevance as evaluated by orthopaedic specialists, and did not include formal readability analysis.

links.outcome: Clinical knowledge accuracy and completeness of LLM answers versus established guidelines
links.effect: Gemini overstated topical medications and arthroscopy for OA, contradicting guidelines; Claude erred on implants and preoperative antibiotics; Q7 and Q9 responses all unacceptable for missing probabilistic data or surgical details.
links.quote: For instance, Google Gemini overstated the effectiveness of topical medications and the role of arthroscopic surgery in osteoarthritis management, contradicting established guidelines.

links.effect: Under zero-shot, ChatGPT-4 had higher accuracy/comprehensiveness than Gemini (P=0.031/0.009) and Claude (P=0.019/0.002).
links.quote: ChatGPT-4 demonstrated significantly higher accuracy and comprehensiveness scores compared to both Google Gemini ( P = 0.031 and P = 0.009, respectively) and Claude 3 Opus ( P = 0.019 and P = 0.002, respectively).

links.outcome: Clinical acceptability of LLM FAQ answers
links.effect: Only 48.8% (156/320) of reviewer ratings deemed responses acceptable; mean accuracy was 3.38 (95% CI 2.67–4.09).
links.quote: Among all responses assessed by the four reviewers, 48.8% (156/320) were deemed acceptable.

unlisted_practices: Use role-playing prompts simulating an experienced orthopaedic surgeon to improve LLM responses to total knee arthroplasty FAQs.

links.outcome: accuracy, comprehensiveness, and acceptability of responses to patient FAQs
links.effect: Role-playing improved ChatGPT-3.5 accuracy (3.70 vs 3.33, P=0.020), comprehensiveness (3.85 vs 3.43, P=0.026), acceptability (72.5% vs 45%, P=0.012), and ChatGPT-4 acceptability (77.5% vs 55%, P=0.033); Gemini and Claude showed no significant changes.
links.quote: When prompted to act as an experienced orthopaedic surgeon specializing in TKA, role-playing significantly improved the performance of ChatGPT-3.5 across all three metrics: accuracy ( P = 0.02), comprehensiveness ( P = 0.026), and acceptability ( P = 0.012) (Table 3 ).
